cryptohome: Reduce needless SecureBlob usage in attestation code. Polymorphic usage of SecureBlob is problematic (see crbug.com/728047). In preparation for making SecureBlob not inherit from Blob (which will break some of these usages), reduce unnecessary use of SecureBlob for non-secrets. There is one use of SecureBlob for the modulus of a public key, and another one for the input to a decryption function. These don't need to be SecureBlobs. Also fix some style issues. CHROMIUM: Fix encrypted characteristic access For characteristic coming with flag "permission-encrypt-read", we only set BT_ATT_PERM_READ_ENCRYPT for now. This will fail the request to encrypted read a characteristic because check_permissions() assumes attributes must be readable/writable (BT_ATT_PERM_READ/BT_ATT_PERM_WRITE) before checking further secure requirements. Thus, this fix could take two different approaches: 1. Modify check_permissions(). If an attribute is encrypted writable, then we don't have to check whether it is writable or not. That is, BT_ATT_PERM_WRITE_ENCRYPT is sufficient to declare that an attribute is writable, without further requirements on BT_ATT_PERM_WRITE. 2. Modify parse_chrc_flags(). This is the approach adopted in this patch. Just make parse_chrc_flags() exactly symmetric to parse_desc_flags(). I adopt 2 because check_permissions() is called in multiple places and it's not easy to modify it safely w/o grasping all the contexts it's called. Besides, approach 2 requires minimal change. As a result, BT_ATT_PERM_.* are still classified into two categories: i) BT_ATT_PERM_READ/BT_ATT_PERM_WRITE for access control ii) Others for security level. A request must meet both access control and security level in order to pass check_permissions(). BUG=b:78593133 TEST=Fix read/write encrypted characteristic on CtsVerifier Change-Id: Ida4ae8f6838ad9a83145b789e00776a2bd984988 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1112059 Commit-Ready: Qiyu Hu <qiyuh@google.com> Tested-by: Qiyu Hu <qiyuh@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com>

CHROMIUM: Fix double bonding_complete() and update bearer select policy new_link_key_callback() and new_long_term_key_callback() are called when keys are generated or received by kernel. Cannot simply assume bonding is complete when we receive keys. During LE secure connection pairing, link key can be derived from long term key for later use (BR/EDR is considered as paired in this case). However, device_bonding_complete should be called only once to report the completion of LE pairing. And the same logic should be applied to BR/EDR pairing. Otherwise, the re-connection will be established based on the wrong device type. Also update the bearer select policy. For dual devices bonded both in BR/EDR and LE, prefer the bearer matching the bdaddr_type. BUG=b:78593133 TEST=Confirm that service discovery occurs only once per pairing Change-Id: Ib29c2c591fe964693c25981956eb56bd2f2f554a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1111570 Commit-Ready: Qiyu Hu <qiyuh@google.com> Tested-by: Qiyu Hu <qiyuh@google.com> Reviewed-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org>

firmware_LockedME: accomodate new flashrom behavior Recent changes to the CrOS version of flashrom result in writes to flash regions protected by the PCH (when instructed by the contents of SI_DESC) to not result in a failed exit status, but still fail to write* (good) and log an access failure (observed on both an Intel big core SoC and Intel small core SoC). The CrOS flashrom maintainer should make some level of effort to couple flashrom behavior changes with faft: so, if the behavior changes back to an exit status of zero, this change should be reverted at the same time (it should be innocuous in that case, but to avoid build up of detritus in this test). *fail to write observation is based on the log of the access failure and read attempts of protected regions still being all ones. BUG=b:110839551, b:110572221 TEST=Ran against a small core DUT (epaullete) with a locked TXE (passed as would be expected). Ran against a big core DUT (pantheon) with the manufacturing mode check commented out (failed as expected with SI_DESC detected as writeable). Change-Id: I83ec216fcb6018961077a3052d54b771a2ec4182 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1116192 Commit-Ready: Kevin Shelton <kmshelton@chromium.org> Tested-by: Kevin Shelton <kmshelton@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Martin Roth <martinroth@chromium.org>

The low memory notification formula should also consider the remaining anonymous memory. Swappable memory is equal to the smaller of swap free and remaining anonymous memory. npcx: adc: only enable ADC during conversion for power consumption. For better power consumption in npcx series ec, this CL only turns on ADC module before starting conversion and turns it off after the conversion is done. If ec enters deep sleep when ADC conversion is ongoing, the conveting process is suspended until next time ec wakes up from the deep sleep. Considering the frequency of ADC's source clock is up to 15MHz, it's more efficient to forbid ec enter deep sleep when the conversion is proceeding. (Each conversion time of ADC channel is ~200us based on this condition.) Forbidding ec enter deep sleep should have no harm. BRANCH=none BUG=b:110170824 TEST=No build errors for npcx7 series. The current of AVCC is reduced from 0.4mA to ~0.01mA on yorp if this patch is applied. Change-Id: Ie9226e942eeefaadbca7c17e45f0b9ee9a2364e9 Signed-off-by: Mulin Chao <mlchao@nuvoton.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1090603 Commit-Ready: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org>
